perspective:
From Ethan’s perspective, what he knows and experienced is:

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my close, long-time friend; we met in middle school. He is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- I invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation. I told him his health is just as important, that I hated seeing him like this, and asked him to go for two days. Gary said he appreciated my concern but couldn’t because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I saw Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected there was more going on than professional obligations. I told him we’d been friends since middle school, he could tell me anything, and I was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me.
- Gary then opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. I felt relief and empathy. I suggested prioritizing his tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and saw him making efforts to change. I felt hopeful and proud. I told him I was proud of his progress and that I was there whenever he needed to talk. Gary said things were better, that my help meant he was less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie.
- After a year, I saw that Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. I felt satisfied and happy for him. I decided to step back but told him I’m always just a call away if he needs anything, and that he’s got this. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and that he felt more in control.
